check.population: every folder and filename under a declared governed root, and every word in the declared vocabularies
check.freshness: a verdict stands until a file is added, moved or renamed, or a vocabulary or root declaration changes
check.refusal: the naming or placement gate fails the lint run on the file, naming the declared word that covers a refused one
check.observation: each path parsed by position against the declared containers, depth cap and closed vocabularies
check.evidence: fires-and-accepts: one suite lints a file whose tag is undeclared and one whose tag differs from its folder, another refuses a repeated role and a path past the depth cap, and both pass conforming paths
check.authority: the declared vocabularies and roots, which every path conforms to, so an undeclared word is an approved edit to the declaration

distinctFrom.reason: A closed vocabulary admits a word only by approved edit, while agnostic-first decides which words to admit, domain-neutral roles before domain ones.

records.name: Closed Vocabulary
records.definition: A design rule that every word in a name slot comes from a declared list, and a new word enters the list only by an approved edit.
detected_by: a name slot holding a word absent from its declared array

exemplar.before: <container>/managers/foo.manager.ts → neither "managers" nor "manager" is a declared word
exemplar.after: <container>/coordinators/foo.coordinator.ts → the declared concern that already covers the role

distinctFrom.reason: Positional slot resolution reads slots from dot-separated segments, while a case dialect reads the same slots from word boundaries in another case.
Positional slot resolution is the reading rule, while the subject slot is one position it reads.
Positional slot resolution is the reading rule, while the variant slot is one position it reads.

records.name: Positional Slot Resolution
records.definition: A mechanism that reads each word of a path by the slot it lands in, so the last dot-segment before a file's extension is always its concern and a folder named after a concern tag resolves as the latest role its depth can legally take.
detected_by: a filename whose last segment before the extension is not a declared concern tag, or a folder carrying a concern tag's label that the resolver places in the subject role
measured_by: unparseable filename count, and folders whose resolved role differs from the latest legal role for their word

exemplar.before: foo-registry.ts → one fused word, so neither slot resolves
exemplar.after: foo.registry.ts → subject "foo", concern "registry"; position decides, so a concern word is legal in the subject slot too

records.name: Concern-Folder Correspondence
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a file's concern tag matches the label of the folder that holds it.
detected_by: tag/folder mismatch on a filesystem walk

exemplar.before: <container>/caches/foo.store.ts → the folder says cache, the tag says store
exemplar.after: <container>/stores/foo.store.ts → the tag terminates the name and names the parent folder

distinctFrom.reason: A glob-resolvable tree is the property that one pattern collects a concern at any depth, while a shape-discovered surface is a consumer that collects by such a pattern.

records.name: Glob-Resolvable Tree
records.definition: A mechanism that lets one unanchored pattern per concern collect every matching file or folder, at whatever depth it sits.
detected_by: a pattern that must enumerate depths to collect one concern

exemplar.before: <root>/*/validators/*.ts and <root>/*/*/validators/*.ts → one pattern per depth, and a new grouping adds another
exemplar.after: **/*.validator.ts for the files, **/validators/ for the folders → two unanchored patterns resolve the concern tree-wide

records.name: Declared Jurisdiction
records.definition: A design rule that a naming gate reads from one declaration the roots it governs, the containers and buckets under each, the classes of file exempt from the grammar, and the trees another system authors or resolves by name, which are exempted once and never governed.
detected_by: a folder at a governed root that is in neither the container nor the bucket declaration
an ignore entry naming authored source that belongs to no exempt class, or a declared root that holds another system's ownership marker
measured_by: ignore entries outside the exempt classes, and exemptions held outside the one upstream declaration
enforced_by: the taxonomy validator, which refuses an ignore entry of wildcards or of a whole extension, and the coordination member's declaration check, which resolves every declared upstream root against the disk and refuses a root carrying a foreign ownership marker

exemplar.before: "a folder holding no folders is a bucket" → inferred, so a container that loses its last folder silently reclassifies and its next loose file passes
exemplar.after: containers{<root>: [...]} + specialContainers{<root>: [...]} → both kinds declared; a folder in neither is flagged

distinctFrom.reason: Bounded nesting depth limits a path, while backward compatibility keeps a new version working for old consumers.
Bounded nesting depth joins two conditions on a path, while the depth cap is the first, the number of folders.
Bounded nesting depth joins two conditions on a path, while the ordered role sequence is the second, the order of roles.

records.name: Bounded Nesting Depth
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a file sits within a fixed number of folders below its governed root, with each folder taking a later role than the one above it.
detected_by: a path over the cap, or a role repeated or revisited along it

exemplar.before: <container>/foo/pools/lru/bar.pool.ts → one folder past the cap, and the extra level resolves to no role at all
exemplar.after: <container>/foo/pools/bar.lru.pool.ts → container, subject, concern, in order and at the cap; the discriminator moved into the variant slot

records.name: Sideways Overflow
records.definition: A design pattern that resolves a naming collision with the filename's variant slot and resolves breadth with a sibling subject folder.
detected_by: a folder level introduced where a variant or a sibling subject folder resolves the collision

exemplar.before: <container>/caches/lru/foo.cache.ts beside <container>/caches/fifo/foo.cache.ts → the collision was relieved by a new level
exemplar.after: <container>/caches/foo.lru.cache.ts beside <container>/caches/foo.fifo.cache.ts → relieved by the variant slot, at the same depth

distinctFrom.reason: One concern per file splits a file that plays two roles, while collision consolidation merges two files that play one.
One concern per file requires a single role, while narrowest concern chooses which declared role names it.

records.name: One Concern Per File
records.definition: A design rule that each file plays exactly one declared role, and a file that plays two is split.
detected_by: a file that classifies equally well under two declared concerns

exemplar.before: foo.store.ts → holds the state AND validates every write, so its concern is two words
exemplar.after: foo.store.ts + foo.validator.ts → the ambiguity was the finding; the split is the fix

records.name: Narrowest Concern
records.definition: A design rule that a file is classified under the narrowest declared role that describes it accurately.
detected_by: one tag carrying files of several distinct roles

exemplar.before: foo.manager.ts → names a stature, so it fits lifecycle owners, caches, registries and coordinators alike
exemplar.after: foo.coordinator.ts → the narrowest declared role that is accurate; a file that cannot choose is doing both

records.name: Layer Spine Precedence
records.definition: A mechanism that breaks an irreducible tie between two roles in favor of the one nearer the domain on the layer spine.
detected_by: an irreducible two-concern overlap resolved by preference rather than by layer

exemplar.before: a file that is irreducibly both is tagged by whichever word came to mind first
exemplar.after: model (domain) beats schema (infrastructure) → domain-ward wins, and only as a tie-break after the split test fails

records.name: Agnostic-First Vocabulary
records.definition: A design rule that a domain-specific role word is admitted only where no domain-neutral role already covers it.
detected_by: a domain tag whose role a declared agnostic concern already covers

exemplar.before: <container>/managers/ and <container>/helpers/ → two catch-all words for roles the agnostic set already names
exemplar.after: <container>/coordinators/ and <container>/predicates/ → a domain tag is admitted only where no agnostic concern covers the role

records.name: Guided Vocabulary Refusal
records.definition: A mechanism that answers a refused word with the declared word that covers its role, looked up in an indexed rejection table.
detected_by: a refusal message naming only the rejected word, and a rejection table readable by the developer but not by the gate
measured_by: share of refusals carrying a resolved replacement

exemplar.before: 'foo.manager.ts' → "'manager' is not a declared concern tag" → the developer guesses again, and the table that already answered this sits in prose no gate reads
exemplar.after: refused word → rejection-table index → "'manager' is covered by 'coordinator'" → foo.coordinator.ts; coverage is decided by the role a file plays, never by a general-language synonym set

records.name: Derived Naming Registry
records.definition: Descriptive data about the declared vocabulary and roots, derived from the naming document so a gate can read it, with the reasoning kept in the document.
detected_by: a tag in the document and absent from the registry, or either way round

exemplar.before: the vocabulary lives only in prose, so every gate re-reads it by hand and a rule written into the config is read by no gate
exemplar.after: document holds the reasoning → registry holds the declarations → one gate and one classifier read the registry; drift either way is a bug

records.name: Set-Relative Member Name
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a file inside a subject folder names only its own subject, because the folder already names the set.
detected_by: a file subject equal to the subject folder above it

exemplar.before: <container>/foo/behaviors/foo-bar.behavior.ts → restates what the folder already said
exemplar.after: <container>/foo/behaviors/bar.behavior.ts → the folder names the set, the file names the member

records.name: Manual Identity Migration
records.definition: A technique for renaming files one container at a time by hand, re-pointing each pattern and comparing what each aggregator collects before and after.
detected_by: a shape-discovered surface whose collected count changed across a rename

exemplar.before: a rename tool rewrites every literal path; **/*.validator.ts now collects nothing and the gate stays green because nothing is left to check
exemplar.after: one container → rename → update every importer → re-point every pattern → compare collected counts against the previous run → gate green before the next container

records.name: Collision Consolidation
records.definition: A design rule that a filename already held by another file is first read as a sign that both files do the same job, and a variant is added only after the code shows that their jobs differ.
detected_by: a variant whose sibling in the same folder shares its concern and one of its responsibilities
measured_by: variants admitted without a consolidation verdict
enforced_by: the duplicates verdict each conversion record carries

exemplar.before: foo.validator.ts exists → the new file becomes foo.extra.validator.ts, and both run the same checks under two names
exemplar.after: the name is taken → both files are read → one job: merged into foo.validator.ts; two jobs: the variant names the facet the code shows

records.name: Mirrored Test Placement
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a test sits in the concern folder of the file it tests, under a test root mirroring that file's governed root, and moves whenever that file moves.
detected_by: a test whose path does not mirror the concern folder of the file it names
enforced_by: the centralized-test and subjectless-test checks, and the taxonomy step's mirror check

exemplar.before: <root>/validators/foo.validator.ts moves to <root>/predicates/foo.predicate.ts → its test stays under the old validators mirror
exemplar.after: <test-root>/predicates/foo.predicate.test.ts → the test moves in the same pass and names the file it now covers

records.name: Sanctioned Generic Subject
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a file takes the one generic subject only when it is generic over its type parameters and names no domain noun anywhere in its source.
detected_by: a file carrying the generic subject whose source names a domain noun
measured_by: generic-subject files that fail either test

exemplar.before: base.cache.ts → holds a cache typed to invoices and sessions, so the generic name hides two subjects
exemplar.after: base.lru.cache.ts for the cache generic over its keys and values, and invoice.cache.ts for the one that names invoices

records.name: Conformance at Creation
records.definition: A design rule that a file created under a governed root is named and placed correctly when it is first written, so no conversion queue accumulates behind new work.
detected_by: a newly created file that the naming or placement gate refuses
measured_by: new files refused on their first run

exemplar.before: a new helper lands as temp.ts, to be renamed later, and three importers bind to the temporary name
exemplar.after: the file is read into its role before it is written → foo.formatter.ts in formatters/ from the first commit

distinctFrom.reason: Registry-held order keeps sequence out of filenames, while declarative configuration keeps settings in validated data.

records.name: Registry-Held Order
records.definition: A design rule that load or execution order is held by an import list or a registry, so a filename carries no numeric prefix the grammar would have to parse.
detected_by: a filename whose first segment is a number

exemplar.before: 01-setup.step.ts, 02-build.step.ts → inserting a step renumbers every name after it
exemplar.after: setup.step.ts, build.step.ts, and the order held once in the registry that runs them

records.name: Externally Resolved Slot
records.definition: A mechanism that resolves a name slot whose words another source owns against that source, whether an index that allocates identities, an upstream key set or a field the file itself carries, so the closed vocabulary never holds a copy of them.
detected_by: a vocabulary entry that mirrors a row of an allocating index, or a corpus file whose facet segment differs from the facet its own field declares
measured_by: slot words held both in the vocabulary and in the source that owns them
enforced_by: the coordination member's slot check, which resolves a seat letter against the index that allocates it

exemplar.before: each new seat letter is added to the variants array → the array and the index disagree as soon as one moves
exemplar.after: the variant slot resolves against the index that allocates letters → a new seat needs no vocabulary edit

records.name: Case Dialect
records.definition: A mechanism that binds file extensions to the case their language names files in and reads the same subject, variant and concern slots from the stem's word boundaries.
detected_by: a dialect file whose trailing words are not a declared concern tag, or a dialect naming a case no splitter reads
measured_by: dialect files that do not resolve to three declared slots
enforced_by: naming gate, which parses a dialect's word run, and the taxonomy validator, which refuses a case no splitter reads

exemplar.before: a language that names files in pascal case falls outside the grammar, so its files are ignored or forced into dotted kebab names its tools do not find
exemplar.after: SessionRefreshValidator.<ext> under a pascal dialect → words session, refresh, validator → subject session, variant refresh, concern validator, and its folder stays kebab

distinctFrom.reason: Root spine files limit which files may sit at a governed root, while the governed root is the declaration that brings a tree under the taxonomy.

records.name: Root Spine Files
records.definition: A rule or precondition that a governed root carries only its entry document and its accumulators at the root, and every other file sits in a concern folder.
detected_by: a loose file at a governed root

exemplar.before: <root>/notes.ts beside <root>/README.md → the loose file resolves to no role
exemplar.after: <root>/README.md and the underscore-marked accumulators stay; every other file moves to <root>/<container>/<concern>/
